posts.cooked:
The last two games were pretty easy victories.  For a real challenge, since you've rolled the Final Wasteland, why don't we fight Akash'Bhuta, who is known to be exceptionally dangerous there?

I'll take Absolute Zero if that's cool.  (Pun not intended.)

Opening hand:  Focused Apertures, Glacial Structure, Cold Snap, Hoarfire.  (Great, no modules.  Guess we know what my first turn will look like.)

Note that if the villain chosen is Plague Rat, the Ennead, or Gloomweaver, or if we switch environments to the Tomb of Anubis, I will have to drop out, as I don't have those decks to reference.  I no longer necessarily need to reference decks, as I'm getting more comfortable with reading the format of these pbp games, but I still feel I should abstain from any game in which I might absolutely need to to look up a card and be unable to do so.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
PlatinumWarlock:

Randomizer be damned, I'm all about the new!

Agreed.  I am a big believer in using randomness as a starting point, but it's perfectly fine to call as many rerolls as necessary until obtaining a satisfactory result, IMO.  The only time you need to "let the dice fall where they may" is when resolving a conflict between two people, who have an equal right to get their own way (whether two people ever have an unequal right is something I frequently change my mind on, although I generally default to saying they never do).
